label: Farcaster
terms_note: Neynar API key on a paid plan; casts consume storage rent (~$7/year per unit = 5,000 casts, oldest pruned). Warpcast spam labels penalise low-quality automation.

auth: 1. Tenant has a Farcaster account (fid). The app needs a **signer**: an Ed25519 key added to the fid via the Key
2. Neynar API key (plans: free tier then paid); `signer_uuid` must be paired with the same API key.

endpoints.call: POST /v2/farcaster/cast/` {signer_uuid, text, embeds[≤ 2 {url}], parent (cast hash or channel URL), channel_id, idem}
Neynar webhooks (cast.created with mention / parent filters)

reference.limits: - Cast text ≤ 1024 bytes UTF-8: `CAST` type 0–320 characters, `LONG_CAST` 321–1024 (protocol spec); ≤ 2 embeds (URLs ≤ 256 bytes); mentions stored as fids + byte positions. - Storage rent: 1 unit ≈ $7/year = 5,000 casts, 2,500 reactions, 2,500 links; oldest pruned beyond the limit (30-day grace after expiry). - Neynar rate limits / pricing follow the plan; Warpcast spam labels reduce reach for low-quality automation.

fields.name: api_key
fields.help: Neynar API key from https://dev.neynar.com: 'All API endpoints require an API key. Include the following header with every request: x-api-key' (https://docs.neynar.com/reference). Writes additionally need a signer (config field signer_uuid) created and approved for the same API key.

config_fields.name: signer_uuid
config_fields.help: UUID of an approved signer for the publishing account ('signer_uuid is paired with API key, can't use a uuid made with a different API key'; 'In order to post a cast signer_uuid must be approved', https://docs.neynar.com/reference/publish-cast). Required for publish_text, reply_comment and delete; env PLATFORM_MCP_FARCASTER_SIGNER_UUID.

config_fields.name: fid
config_fields.help: Farcaster id (integer) of the connected account, used by `me` (GET /v2/farcaster/user/bulk/?fids=) and read_mentions (GET /v2/farcaster/notifications/?fid=); env PLATFORM_MCP_FARCASTER_FID.

adapter.rate_note: Neynar meters requests per minute by subscription plan (the endpoint references state no numbers) and answers 429 when exceeded; one client-side bucket at 5/s.

me.note: GET /v2/farcaster/user/bulk/?fids=<fid> ('Comma separated list of FIDs, up to 100 at a time') returns BulkUsersResponse {users[{fid, username, display_name, custody_address, follower_count, following_count, profile{bio}, verifications, ...}]}; the connected account is account.users[0]. This verifies the API key and describes the configured fid; it does not prove the signer is approved.

publish_text.note: POST /v2/farcaster/cast/ {signer_uuid (required, 'UUID of the signer'), text, parent?} returns {success, cast{hash, author{fid}, text}}; `id` is the cast hash (0x-prefixed, used by read_comments / delete / analytics_post). `reply_to` is sent as `parent` ('parent URL of channel or hash of cast being replied to'), so it may be a cast hash or a channel URL; channel_id, embeds and idem are not sent. No url / created_at in the response.

read_comments.note: GET /v2/farcaster/cast/conversation/?identifier=<hash>&type=hash&reply_depth=1&limit=N ('Cast identifier (It's either a URL or a hash)'; reply_depth 0-5, default 2; limit 1-50, default 20; sort_type default chron) returns {conversation{cast{..., direct_replies[{hash, author{fid, username}, text, timestamp, direct_replies[]}]}, chronological_parent_casts}, next{cursor}}; `comments` are the direct replies. Pagination is cursor-based, so `page` is not sent.

reply_comment.note: A reply is a cast whose `parent` is the comment's hash ('parent URL of channel or hash of cast being replied to'); parent_author_fid is optional and not sent. Needs the approved signer_uuid.

read_mentions.note: GET /v2/farcaster/notifications/?fid=<configured fid>&type=mentions&limit=N (type is an array parameter of follows | recasts | likes | mentions | replies | quotes, sent as the single value mentions; limit 1-25, default 15) returns {unseen_notifications_count, notifications[{type, most_recent_timestamp, seen, cast{hash, author{username}, text, timestamp}}], next{cursor}}. Cursor pagination, so `page` and `since` are not sent. Neynar recommends webhooks for bot mentions ('It's more real time and cheaper compute').

delete.note: DELETE /v2/farcaster/cast/ with a JSON body {signer_uuid (required), target_hash (required, the cast hash)} returns {success, message} (the runtime answers {status: 'deleted'}; the upstream body is under raw). 'In order to delete a cast signer_uuid must be approved', and the signer must belong to the cast's author.

analytics_post.note: GET /v2/farcaster/cast/?identifier=<hash>&type=hash returns CastResponse {cast{hash, author, text, timestamp, reactions{likes_count, recasts_count}, replies{count}, embeds, ...}}. The runtime cannot compose a nested `metrics` object, so counts are top-level fields (likes, recasts, replies).

publish_image.note: POST /v2/farcaster/cast/ {signer_uuid, text?, embeds: [{url}]}: `embeds` is an array with maxItems 2 of URL embeds ({url: string}) or cast embeds ({cast_id: {fid, hash}}), so the first TWO image_urls are sent as URL embeds and any further ones are ignored; Farcaster clients render image URLs inline. `id` is the cast hash; no url / created_at in the response. Needs the approved signer_uuid.

evidence: probe: 8/8 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
